learningObjective: Understand persistent-kernel pattern: fixed blocks + internal work-stealing loop for launch-overhead amortization.

canonicalClaims.claim: A persistent CUDA kernel launches a fixed number of blocks (matched to hardware occupancy) and loops internally over work items pulled from a global counter/queue; the pattern amortizes kernel-launch overhead across many small work items and gives the kernel manual control over scheduling.
conditions: Work items are numerous and short; atomicAdd is available.
nonImplications: Does not imply persistent kernels always win over many-launch approaches.
Does not imply CUDA provides a `__persistent__` attribute.

misconceptions.whyWrong: No such attribute exists; the pattern is an idiom.

misconceptions.claim: Persistent kernels must be killed via `cudaKillKernel`.
misconceptions.whyWrong: No such API; kernels self-terminate via exit condition.

misconceptions.claim: Persistent kernels only work on Grace-Hopper CPUs.
Persistent kernels eliminate all overhead, including per-work-item atomicAdd cost.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Work-stealing atomics have their own contention cost; the pattern trades one overhead for another.

implementationFacts: Common in LLM decoding, small-tile GEMM tail handling, custom schedulers.
